tool.title: Instantiate a harness over a repository that has none: pin, mount, open the setup-only PR, render the preview
tool.description: The scripted step of the initiation process (getting-started.bpmn, the repo-conversion skill §4). Reads the harness's declaration at its pin and every `needs`, transitively (a need beside the layer that needs it unless --repo-of says otherwise, at its default branch's tip unless --pin says otherwise, its declaration's name checked), seeds them all into the repository's index.config.json with the consent given (`remote-mount --seed --whole`), sets `site.landing` to the harness, `site.agentRun` and `mountApprovers`, mounts the closure (`remote-mount`: index.lock.json and the .gitignore mounts block), installs it as root workspaces with the hoisted linker, writes the root bootstrap (`.github/cat.ts` and `.github/mount-from-lock.sh` from cat-harness-tools `templates/root-bootstrap/`) and sets the root's `cat` script to `bun .github/cat.ts`, so `bun run cat …` mounts the layers itself on a later fresh clone, re-renders the agent surface from the mounted generators, runs the harness's `instantiate:<harness>` checkout script when a mounted layer declares it, and commits on a branch (default harness/<harness>). Then, unless --local, pushes the branch, provisions gh-pages when absent (`pages-bootstrap --provision`), opens the setup-only PR, runs `prepare:<harness>` when declared (what the site is built from and nobody commits, such as an IG's AST) and renders the branch's preview at gh-pages branches/<branch>/ (`stage-local`); with --local the site is built and composed and nothing is pushed. It imports only node:*, so it runs from a fresh clone of cat-harness-tools before anything is mounted: it lays the platform's own closure, at the pins the repository will mount, into a temporary root to run the mount from. On a repository with nothing mounted yet, run the same file from a fresh clone: `git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/litlfred/cat-harness-tools /tmp/cht && bun run /tmp/cht/scripts/instantiate-harness.ts …`. Two more flags, not declared as ports because no constrained type carries them yet: `--pin <name>=<sha>` pins one layer of the closure, `--repo-of <name>=<owner/repo>` says where a need lives.

inputs.name: repo
inputs.description: The checkout to harness: clean, with a GitHub origin. Default: the working directory.

inputs.name: harness
inputs.description: The harness, OWNER/REPO, pinned at its default branch's tip (pin it otherwise with --pin <name>=<sha>).

inputs.name: consentBy
inputs.description: Who consented to mounting the closure; also recorded as the one mountApprover. The evidence (where they consented, readable) is read from stdin.

inputs.name: evidence
inputs.description: Where the consent was given, readable (a session, an issue comment). On stdin because it is free prose: it quotes what was said.

inputs.name: branch
inputs.description: The setup branch. Default: harness/<harness>. Never the default branch.

inputs.name: plan
inputs.description: Resolve the closure, print every step, and stop.

inputs.name: local
inputs.description: Commit on the branch, push nothing; the site is built and composed (stage-local --dry-run).

inputs.name: noPr
inputs.description: Push the branch and the preview, open no PR.

outputs.name: url
outputs.description: The branch's preview, gh-pages branches/<branch>/, once GitHub's Pages deploy has run.

render.reason: a reader opens the preview; the scheme is checked before it reaches an href

selection.when: A repository that mounts no harness yet is to be harnessed: an existing FHIR IG adopting a FHIR harness, a repository becoming a folio overlay. Its PR is the setup-only PR repo-conversion §4 asks for before any content PR.
selection.limits: The harness's own adoption steps are its checkout scripts instantiate:<harness> and prepare:<harness>; a harness that declares neither is mounted and rendered with what its layers already declare, and a site that needs a build input nobody produced (an IG with no AST) is refused by the render step with its reason. Re-pinning an already harnessed repository is remote-mount --seed, not this.
selection.cost: The mount: a blobless fetch of each layer of the closure and one install (a few minutes). Then the harness's prepare step (an IG's AST: a full IG Publisher run) and the render.

remedies.none: The closure is fetched from GitHub and the branch, preview and PR are pushed there; offline nothing can be pinned.
